explain.say: Before dawn on 1 September 1939, German forces invaded Poland. Two days later Britain and France declared war. Nearly six years later, Soviet soldiers raised their flag over the Reichstag in Berlin. Look at the timeline of the war in Europe. We will follow its turning points, and remember its victims.

explain.say: Now the map. Germany's blitzkrieg, lightning war with tanks and aircraft together, defeated France in about six weeks in 1940. Britain fought on alone and won the Battle of Britain in the air. Then on 22 June 1941 Hitler invaded the Soviet Union with about three million German troops. Why was a war on two fronts so risky for Germany?

Behind the front, Nazi Germany carried out the Holocaust, the murder of about six million Jews, around two thirds of Europe's Jews, in mass shootings and in death camps such as Auschwitz-Birkenau and Treblinka. In January 1942 officials met at Wannsee to coordinate it. Roma, disabled people, Soviet prisoners and others were also murdered. We remember each of them.

explain.say: The tide turned in the east. In February 1943 a whole German army surrendered at Stalingrad. On 6 June 1944 Allied troops landed in Normandy, and Germany surrendered on 8 May 1945. See the reasons historians like Richard Overy give: Soviet sacrifice, American industry, Hitler's overreach, codebreaking. Which side of Germany saw most of the fighting?

explain.say: Look at the human cost, all estimates: about 27 million Soviet citizens, about 6 million Poles, half of them Jewish, about 7 million Germans, and many more across Europe. Each figure is millions of single lives. Thank you for thinking carefully. Exam tip: give the Eastern Front its full weight, alongside D-Day.

faq.q: Why did the Allies win the Second World War in Europe?
faq.a: Historians such as Richard Overy point to the Soviet Union's huge manpower and sacrifice on the Eastern Front, American industrial output and Lend-Lease, Hitler's strategic overreach, Allied codebreaking and command of sea and air, and resistance across occupied Europe.

The systematic, state-organised murder of about six million Jews by Nazi Germany and its collaborators between 1941 and 1945, through mass shootings, ghettos, starvation and death camps such as Auschwitz-Birkenau. Roma, disabled people, Soviet prisoners of war and others were also murdered.
asks: How many people died in the Holocaust?

faq.q: Why was Stalingrad a turning point?
faq.a: In February 1943 the German Sixth Army, encircled at Stalingrad, surrendered. It was a huge loss of men and prestige, and afterwards the Red Army mostly advanced west. Most German military deaths in the war came on the Eastern Front.

faq.q: How many people died in the Second World War in Europe?
faq.a: Estimates are uncertain, but about 27 million Soviet citizens died, about 6 million people in Poland, about 7 million Germans, and millions more elsewhere, soldiers and civilians together. The war worldwide killed around 70 to 85 million people.

On 6 June 1944 about 156,000 American, British, Canadian and other Allied troops landed on the Normandy coast of France, opening a western front that, with the Soviet advance, defeated Germany within a year.

facts: Germany invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941.
Germany's surrender took effect on 8 May 1945.
